name: Shakti caudate signal, left parietal lobe ('arousal', 30 min)
summary: Murphy's caudate nucleus ('body') signal over the left parietal lobe only, which he describes as arousing: energy and excitement, possibly anger or sexual desire.
setting: Darkness and quiet (the vendor says effects during a session need darkness and silence); eyes closed, relaxed, without meditating or falling asleep; no meditation, mind machines or drugs at the same time.
schedule: Vendor's Shakti rules: at most every 72 h or once a week, never on consecutive days; a series of 3 or 6 sessions, then a 21-day break; try a session 2-3 times before changing it. Keep to it even though parietal thresholds are higher, and stay with parietal placement for the whole series.
notes: Coils over the parietal strip, which the vendor locates 'about an inch behind the topmost point on the head, and then in a strip down to the top of the ears': CP1, CP3, CP5 and P3 on the left (an inference); the right channels stay unused. All four coils of the side run together; the 8-coil channel alternation is not used, as with the 2- and 4-coil Shakti. The caudate signal is unpublished, and Murphy calls it 'not a well tested signal'; the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz, 230 points of 3 ms = 0.69 s, then Shakti's standard 4 s of silence) stands in for it, as in the project's Shiva caudate session, so the waveform here does not differ from the amygdala stand-in. Murphy describes 'intense tingly sensations ... sensations of movement' with parietal sessions, left-side caudate sessions as arousing (energy, excitement, possibly anger or sexual desire) and right-side ones as relaxing (calm, possibly lethargy), and bilateral ones as balancing body awareness; these are vendor reports. Murphy names anger among the possible effects of the left side; stop if irritable or angry. Other forms: murphy-shakti-caudate-parietal-right (relaxation) and the bilateral -bilateral-fast and -bilateral-slow. The vendor says thresholds over the parietal lobes 'are a bit higher' and asks users to keep to the normal schedules and not to switch back and forth between the parietal lobes and other locations. A report of anger in two users after a left caudate session followed by a left amygdala session is credited to Murphy but could not be verified on his pages (including both caudate pages); as a precaution, do not follow a left caudate session with a left amygdala session. The vendor does not suggest the caudate signal over the frontal lobes in the 2- and 4-coil Shakti. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012, the latter with the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal). Not for people with epilepsy; stop at once if distressed.
